purpose: Assesses whether the organization can detect an adversary's attempts to avoid detection by AI-enabled security software throughout a compromise.
summary: Defense Evasion consists of techniques adversaries use to avoid detection throughout their compromise, including evading AI-enabled security software such as malware or anomaly detectors through adversarial perturbation or other manipulation designed to blind or bypass AI-based defenses.
expectedStatementElements: Whether AI-enabled security tools (malware/anomaly/fraud detection) are tested against adversarial evasion techniques
How the organization monitors for signs that AI-based detection systems are being systematically probed or bypassed
What layered, non-AI-dependent detection controls exist so evasion of one AI-based control doesn't grant free rein
How model behavior drift is monitored as a potential indicator of evasion attempts
evidenceExamples: Adversarial evasion testing results against AI-based security/detection tools
Monitoring and alerting configuration for systematic probing of detection systems
Documentation of defense-in-depth controls that don't solely rely on AI-based detection
Model behavior drift monitoring reports or dashboards
commonGaps: AI-based security tools have never been tested against adversarial evasion techniques
Detection relies solely on AI-based tools with no non-AI fallback or layered control
No monitoring exists for behavior drift that could indicate an ongoing evasion attempt
interviewQuestions: Have we tested whether our AI-based security tools can be fooled by adversarial inputs?
If someone found a way to blind our AI-based detection, do we have any non-AI backstop?
Would we notice if someone was systematically probing our detection systems to find a bypass?
How do we monitor for gradual drift in model behavior that might signal evasion in progress?
